gateCoverage.encoderFilter: Only gates directly on semantic input/lineage, prefill caller, decoder parity, prefill quality, and promotion were included from the very large neural-prefill ledger. Unrelated latent training, QLoRA, lexical, storage cleanup, and broad corpus tasks were not reclassified.
gateCoverage.kvFilter: Only active model/runtime cache identity, prefix reuse, and the sampled ACE packet revision gates were included. QLoRA/adaptation, Code Mode, MCP operations, and unrelated packet format experiments remain outside this critical path.
gateCoverage.pcaSvdFilter: Reviewed for dependency/ownership overlap; its 11 unchecked tasks are not prerequisites for the selected prefill/cache slice. PCA/SVD remains an optional derived-representation challenger behind identity, artifact, and quality gates.

summary.interpretation: The ledgers mix executable gates with explicit deferrals and governance criteria. PROVEN is scoped to the exact receipt/contract claim, not production promotion. OPTIONAL_RESEARCH is not a blocker for the selected vertical slice.

semanticIdentity.owner: canonical source/chunk and candidate lineage contracts
semanticIdentity.rule: An execution/cache ID or CandidateOrdinal does not replace canonical identity. Missing source/workspace lineage blocks semantic admission.

representation.owner: semantic representation/embedding contract and its immutable artifact receipt
representation.rule: semantic_768 is the canonical logical representation; PCA/SVD/latent outputs are derived representations and cannot repair or redefine semantic identity.

execution.owner: existing prefill/decoder caller and runtime-specific executors
execution.rule: The neural decoder caller is a shadow execution seam. CPU, CUDA, LibTorch, TensorRT, and llama-server execution receipts are not representation or identity owners.

cacheAndBitFrostControl.owner: revision/checksum-qualified BitFrost/Valkey descriptors and residency policy
cacheAndBitFrostControl.rule: Cache metadata may select or describe reusable prompt prefixes; it is not canonical content or model state. No arbitrary KV tensor, hidden reasoning, or recurrent state is persisted.

modelMemory.rule: Keep these three runtime state classes distinct; do not treat server prompt-cache reuse as portable model memory or a BitFrost payload.

overlapReconciliation.finding: Neural-prefill and prefill/residency converge at the existing prefill identity and decoder caller; they are not separate decoder or cache owners.

The one low-level neural decoder caller is already used by the shadow wrapper and the OAK DAG latent handler. Both call the same function in SHADOW_READONLY mode; do not add a second HTTP client/caller.

A live shadow caller receipt exists, but it proves bounded shadow replay only. The separate readiness receipt is older and reports missing caller identity; reconcile by treating the newer shadow proof as caller-path evidence, while retaining canonical lineage and production promotion blocks.

GPU residency policy and lease contracts exist, but cross-executor claimant accounting is explicitly NOT_YET_WIRED; the policy fixture does not prove process-wide VRAM reservation or pre-OOM enforcement.

Prefill routing has a current control-plane candidate, but the reconciled report records a tensor-width conflict and PrefillRoutingDecisionV1 status NOT_DEFINED. Do not introduce a second RetrievalPlan owner.

Existing ContextPrefixIdentityV1 is the prefix identity contract to reconcile against; a separately named OrnithPrefixIdentityV1 should not be created as a duplicate. Runtime cache reuse remains a separate measured observation.

The current semantic input work is not automatically production eligible: prior canaries used provisional first-4000-character truncation, which is not a frozen content-selection policy; exact embedded bytes must be bound before scale-up.

existingNeuralDecoderCaller.modes: Both production-facing wrappers call the shared seam in SHADOW_READONLY mode; environment/identity checks can return no result, and decoder failure preserves the original prefill checksum.
existingNeuralDecoderCaller.focusedTests: The caller spec covers disabled mode, unavailable/rejected decoder, HIT/MISS, stable resolved prefill checksum, and repeat HIT behavior. Tests were inspected, not rerun in this read-only pass.

liveReceipt.scopeLimit: One shadow replay receipt; not production decoder promotion, full current lineage, or GPU/native parity.

existingNeuralDecoderCaller.decision: Reuse this caller. Do not propose or implement another decoder caller.

oneSmallestCompleteVerticalSlice.title: Read-only runtime cache-state and active-model capability receipt
oneSmallestCompleteVerticalSlice.whyThisSlice: It is the smallest end-to-end check across the overlapping prefill/memory boundary that reuses an existing owner, needs no inference, and can return a useful fail-closed result without touching canonical stores or enabling a feature.
prerequisites: Use the existing probeOrnithCacheCapabilityV1 implementation and schema; do not add a second capability owner.
Read active llama-server model/build metadata and configured cache flags without issuing a generation request.
Record modelSha256 as null/UNPROVEN if the runtime cannot provide an immutable artifact digest; never infer it from a mutable model name.
Classify attention KV tensors, model-specific recurrent state, and server-managed prompt/prefix cache as separate runtime-owned state.
Receipt must state writesPerformed=false, canonicalAuthority=false, inferencePerformed=false, and no tensor/state payload persisted.
oneSmallestCompleteVerticalSlice.expectedExit: CAPABILITY_OBSERVED_WITH_EXPLICIT_UNPROVEN_FIELDS or BLOCKED_RUNTIME; either is a complete read-only diagnostic outcome, not production readiness.
